facts: A process model for hierarchical perceptual sound organization is proposed.
The process model recognizes perceptual sounds included in incoming sound signals.
Perceptual sound organization is considered as a scene analysis problem in the auditory domain.
The model consists of multiple processing modules.
The model consists of a hypothesis network for quantitative integration of multiple sources of information.
When input information for each processing module is available, the module rises to process it.
Output information is asynchronously written to the hypothesis network.
On the hypothesis network, individual information is integrated.
On the hypothesis network, an optimal internal model of perceptual sounds is automatically constructed.
A music scene analysis system has been developed based on the model.
The music scene analysis system is for acoustic signals of ensemble music.
The music scene analysis system recognizes rhythm.
The music scene analysis system recognizes chords.
The music scene analysis system recognizes source-separated musical notes.
Experimental results show that a method has permitted autonomous, stable and effective information integration to construct the internal model of hierarchical perceptual sounds.
